title: Few early friends, a flood and the family piano
summary: He remembers little about friends before age 12, living in Youngstown, a flood, his father's library, and always having a piano at home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When you were in school, this is in Columbus, did you make friends easily?

Well, this is -- I don't remember ever having any trouble making friends. I don't remember ever having a lot of good friends during that time. That's a little bit too early for me to remember. I -- my memory as far as remembering friends and things of that sort didn't start until I was 12 years old, precisely, when we were later on living in

another city, another state. But these periods of my early childhood, which I'm trying to remember as much as possible of, were at my mother's death and just after that. Which as I said I can't even remember the towns, all of the towns. I know we lived in Youngstown, Ohio, and during this same time I'd say the period between five and 12 I spent some time in one city where there was a terrible flood, and I remember it was very interesting to me as a boy to remember back how the people were going down the street in boats, and the water was up to the first floor of our house. And many of my father's important books and bibles and so forth got all wet and these things I remember because it's associated also with moving. Because these things I seem to recollect more than anything, and that is the moving, the consistent moving.

And my father had quite a library of books, encyclopedias and Christian bibles and material on teaching and literature. And of course I would always have to remember that we always had a piano in the front room, because my mother played, and everybody in the family played music.
